question: Q9
raw_text:
Real world examples of outlier detections.
- Network Intrusion Detection
  → A user suddenly accesses 100,000 request (DDOS) per sec
  → record from a single IP (cybersecurity)
- Collective outliers (Normal individually, abnormal as pattern over time)
- Fake news
  → Article mixes with unrelated claims
  → Contextual outlier (the sentence is odd given the situation).

Does AI detect outliers better than statistical/posing methods?
→ it depends heavily on what data type and task.

One common example:
• AI → 2200 shot defection ⇒ Can flag anomalies on aero training data on what 'normal' looks like.

Methods → No hallucination risk ⇒ AI can confidently identify something as outlier even often it's not. Statistical/proximity methods don't have this.

* Apart from that, the computational cost for these methods are commonly higher than using AI, since AI used already a pretrained model or they can apply various method (knowledge distillation/transfer learning).
cleaned_text: Real-world examples: network intrusion detection (a user suddenly making 100,000 requests/sec - DDoS - from a single IP), collective outliers (normal individually, abnormal as a pattern over time), and fake news (an article mixing unrelated claims - a contextual outlier). Whether AI detects outliers better than statistical/proximity methods depends heavily on the data type and task. AI has a hallucination risk - it can confidently call something an outlier even when it isn't - which statistical/proximity methods don't. However, AI often has lower computational cost since it uses a pretrained model or methods like knowledge distillation/transfer learning.
